title: Gas flow and accretion via spiral streamers and circumstellar disks in a young binary protostar
question: How does gas flow from the circumbinary disk onto the circumstellar disks and the two protostars in the young binary [BHB2007] 11, and which component accretes preferentially?

data.bands: Band 6 (225.3 GHz, 1.3 mm); Band 3 (97.5 GHz) continuum also used

what.value: Previous ALMA CO(2-1)/H2CO data and Band 3 data

evidence.quote: Using the molecular line data reported in ( _8, 11_ ), we performed two-dimensional Gaussian

external_data.citation: Alves et al. 2017 (cite 8); Alves et al. 2018 (cite 11)

recipe.method: Gaussian fit to 225.3 GHz map; inclination from axis ratio
Modified blackbody, Eq. S8, optically thin/thick cases
assumptions: κ250GHz = 1.7 cm2/g dust, gas-to-dust 100, Tdust ~110 K at 3 au (1.75 Lsun each); filament Tdust 40-100 K

recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fits per channel for peak positions; Keplerian fit to H2CO PV diagram

recipe.goal: Accretion rate, Toomre Q, ionized mass loss
recipe.method: Free-fall accretion estimate; Q approximation; Anglada jet formula with VLA free-free flux
assumptions: jet θ=10°, v=200 km/s, T=1e4 K; M*≈1.0 Msun; 15% flux error

evidence.quote: of 2.25 ± 0.13 M ⊙, which represents an upper limit
the circumbinary disk mass is 0.08 ± 0.03 M ⊙ .

not_stated_but_needed: Self-calibration solution intervals and number of rounds
Clean threshold, mask and image size/cell size
Continuum-free channels used for line cubes
Details of line cube imaging for CO and H2CO
Circumbinary disk mass inputs from Alves 2017
score_reason: Public data and main parameters given, but self-cal, line imaging details and some assumptions are incomplete.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, stated imaging parameters and numeric results (sizes, masses, fluxes) can be redone.
